title: Motivated Decision Withdrawal of Charge C25-0040 2025FT21 DENALI QH - Mr Fahad WALEED (APR)
text:
REASONED DECISION WITHDRAWING CHARGES
RENDERED BY THE FEI TRIBUNAL
29 June 2026
(OPERATIVE DECISION WITHDRAWING CHARGES ISSUED 21 MAY 2026)
In the matter of
FÉDÉRATION EQUESTRE INTERNATIONALE (the “FEI”)
vs.
Mr. Fahad WALEED - Additional Person Responsible (Trainer) - (Ref. C25-0040) (the “APR”)
together the “Parties”
(Reference No. FEI Tribunal: C25-0040 (FEI Case number: Case 2025/FT21 DENALI QH)
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Ms. Diane Pitts, (USA), Sole Panel Member
FEI Tribunal Reference: C25-0040 [FEI 2025/FT21 DENALI QH]
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Majed ALQAHTANI/10363591/KSA
Trainer/ID/NF: Fahad WALEED/10306368/KSA
Event/Date: CEI1* 100 - Riyadh (KSA), 24-26.04.2025
Event/Code: 2025_CI_0266_E_S_02
Date of sample collection: 26.04.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Triamcinolone Acetonide
Bar Code Nos.: 1417731

I. Introduction
1. On 28 April 2026, the FEI Tribunal issued a decision (the Original Decision) in which Mr.
Fahad Waleed, as the Registered Trainer of the horse, DENALI QH, FEI ID 109AP47 (the
Horse), received a suspension relating to the positive finding of Triamcinolone Acetonide
in a sample taken from the Horse at CEI1* 100 - Riyadh (KSA), 24-26.04.2025 (the Event).
Mr. WALEED (the Additional Person Responsible or APR) was notified of the positive
finding by the FEI and the potential penalties under Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping
& Controlled Medication Rules (the EADCMRs) on 19 May 2025. No response was
received by the FEI from the APR at the time the charge was notified nor at any time
thereafter prior to the issuance of the Original Decision on 28 April 2026 pursuant to
which MR. WALEED received a suspension for a period of six (6) months, a fine of three
thousand, five hundred Swiss Francs (CHF 3’500) and legal costs of two thousand Swiss
Francs (CHF 2’000).
2. Subsequent to the publication of the Original Decision, the FEI and the FEI Tribunal (the
Tribunal) were informed on 7 May 2026 by the APR that at the date of the sample
collection and alleged violation, he was not, in fact, the Registered Trainer of the Horse in
the FEI database.
3. Therefore, on 7 May 2026 the APR requested that this matter be reviewed and that his
position and responsibility during the relevant period be taken into consideration.
4. Applicable Rules Provisions
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List).
▪ FEI 2024 Endurance Rules, 12th Edition, effective 1 January 2024 (ERs).
5. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not otherwise
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
2

II. Factual background
6. The FEI (together with the APR, the Parties), is the sole IOC-recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage and para-dressage, jumping, eventing, driving and para-driving,
endurance, and vaulting.
7. The Tribunal notes that at the time of the Original Decision, it was informed by the FEI that
the APR, a registered Trainer from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (the KSA-NF), was the
registered Trainer for the Horse, which competed with its rider Mr. Majed ALQAHTANI (the
Person Responsible or the PR) FEI ID: 10363591, at the Event. Under Article 2.1 of the
EADCMRs, a registered trainer of a horse in the discipline of Endurance in a competition is
considered an Additional Person Responsible (APR) for violations of the EADCMRs .
8. As mentioned at paragraph 1, subsequent to the issuance of the Original Decision, the
APR informed the FEI that he was not the Registered Trainer at the time of the violation.
Further to which the FEI informed the Tribunal via email on 11 May 2026 that following a
review of the information recorded in the FEI database, the FEI confirmed that Mr Waleed,
the APR, was not the Registered Trainer at the time of the sample collection.
9. As such, the Tribunal considered the facts submitted and issued an Operative Decision
on 21 May 2026 in respect of these proceedings, and set aside the Decision including the
findings and sanctions imposed on the APR.
III. Terms of the Decision
10. As a result, the FEI Tribunal Panel (the Panel) confirms the following decision originally
issued on 21 May 2026:
a) The Panel hereby sets aside the finding (dated 28 April 2026) of the violation of Article
2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations (the “EADCMRs”)
against Mr. Fahad WALEED (APR);
b) The Panel lifts the Suspension imposed on the APR effective immediately;
c) The Panel sets aside the fine imposed on the APR;
d) The Panel sets aside the order for costs imposed on the APR;
e) This Decision is notified to the APR, to the FEI and to Equestrian Federation of Saudi
Arabia.
3

FOR THE TRIBUNAL
_________________________________________________________
Ms Diane Pitts, Sole Panel Member
